how_the_number_is_read: PARSED NUMERICALLY off the named maximum lines. checkMesh's OWN VERDICT LINES ARE CAPTURED AND DISCARDED into a field named verdict_line_IGNORED_NEVER_A_GATE. This is not a precaution against a hypothetical: cases/committee-grids/logs/DPW5_hex_checkMesh.log prints `Non-orthogonality check OK.` at a PARSED maximum of 89.7134 degrees, and the same string appears on the prism, hybrid and HLPW6 logs at 89.9441, 89.9985 and 89.9835. Planted control C7 asserts exactly that pairing before any measurement counts. Aspect ratio is read from BOTH checkMesh label forms: the `=` form (`Max aspect ratio = 805.199 OK.`) and the `:` form (`***High aspect ratio cells found, Max aspect ratio: 14426.8`). A reader matching only `=` sees the healthy logs and silently misses exactly the pathological ones; control C5 feeds it one of each and requires a non-null value from both.
planted_controls: Rule 3 and frozen registration section 7. ELEVEN controls, ALL RUN BEFORE ANY CONVERSION, so a control failure costs ZERO core-minutes -- the driver runs `analyse_rung0.py --controls-only` first and stops at exit 5 if any fails. TEN FIRED GREEN against real artifacts before this entry was written; the eleventh is honestly NOT RUN. C0 (x2, one per file layout) is an ABSOLUTE control on a synthetic UGRID this comparator writes byte by byte -- it exists because every other control is DIFFERENTIAL, and a reader returning a constant WRONG answer would move correctly around all of them. C1 renames a .mapbc group in a scratch copy and requires the new name in the emitted set. C2 deletes one boundary face from a scratch copy of the real DPW5 hex grid, rewriting the header count, the connectivity, the tag and both Fortran record markers, and requires exactly one patch's count to drop by exactly 1 with cells unchanged (measured: symmetry 15360 -> 15359, bnd 41984 -> 41983, cells 638976 unchanged). C3 adds 1 to one nFaces in a scratch polyMesh boundary and requires R0-G2a to report UNEQUAL. C4 renames a patch and requires a name-set mismatch. C5 is the two label forms. C6 requires a non-trivial derived cell-volume ratio from a log where Min != Max volume. C7 is the verdict-line trap. C8 requires an absent log to read ABSENT and yield no number -- ABSENT NEVER READS CLEAN. C9, section 7's foam_to_ugrid round-trip plant, is NOT RUN and says so: the writer does not exist, so the control is neither passed nor failed, it is UNBUILT.
two_defects_the_controls_caught_before_a: Recorded because they are the case for controls-before-compute rather than an embarrassment to bury. (1) The reader's Fortran offset was 4 and should be 8 -- a .r8.ugrid is TWO Fortran unformatted records, so the header is followed by its own trailing marker AND the data record's leading marker. The wrong offset read boundary tags of [660176, 657041, 654993] on the three DPW5 grids and the unnamed-tag refusal caught it. HLPW6 is a raw C stream and was never affected, so A READER TESTED ON ONE GRID WOULD HAVE SHIPPED THIS DEFECT. (2) C2's plant deleted NOTHING: it removed 'the first boundary triangle' and DPW5 L1.T hex has nTri = 0, every one of its 41,984 boundary faces being a quad. The planted file came out byte-identical in size to the source, and a control that quietly does nothing certifies a reader that can see nothing. The plant now checks its own byte arithmetic before the reader is asked anything.
reader_independence: Section 4's R0-G2a requires an independent reader, 'not ugrid_to_foam.py, and not importing it'. cases/committee-grids/read_ugrid_identity.py carries its OWN self-validating layout sniffer, its OWN header arithmetic and its OWN .mapbc parser, and shares no constant with the converter. The pre-existing cases/committee-grids/inspect_ugrid.py DOES `from ugrid_to_foam import sniff_layout` and is therefore unusable for R0-G2a; that is why a new reader exists rather than the old one being wired up. The reader was validated against the FROZEN section 3 table on all four grids and reproduces every figure exactly, including HLPW6's fourteen per-patch face counts summing to 149,789.
